text: Fighting for universal healthcare, strong public schools, and safer streets.

Adopted by a single mom from an orphanage in Kolkata ("Calcutta"), India, Jeremy made history as the first Asian-American elected to state office from Upstate New York — and is the first Rochester City Schools graduate in the State Senate in decades.

Born in India, but raised in Rochester's South Wedge neighborhood, Jeremy attended city schools, earned scholarships to college and law school, and has worked in the public, private, and nonprofit sectors. He was elected to the state senate in 2020, now proudly representing his hometown.

As the son of a union teacher, education has always been a priority. He graduated from Rochester's School of the Arts as a vocal music major, earning his B.A. with honors from Hobart & William Smith Colleges — where he served as student body president — and received his J.D. from Albany Law School, where he was class president and a member of the editorial board for the Albany Law Review.

Jeremy's public service began in the early 2000's when he worked for late U.S. Congresswoman Louise Slaughter, whose constituent-service ethic shaped his entire career. He has worked for two New York Governors and served as the chief of staff for Rochester City Hall.

Since taking office, Jeremy secured tax cuts for middle-class New Yorkers, delivered record funding for public schools, and helped author the New York CHIPS Act — creating an economic development program that brought Micron and other semiconductor companies, and thousands of jobs, to Upstate New York. He is the chair of the Senate's Transportation Committee, where he leads infrastructure and mobility policy across New York State.
Jeremy is married to Dr. Diane, a surgeon with the University of Rochester Medical Center. Together they reside in the City of Rochester and are raising their young son.

Secured $162M in accelerated middle-class tax cuts and championed expanded child tax credits — up to $1,000 per child — to break the cycle of poverty.

We can make healthcare more affordable and accessible to all by taking bold action. I want to pass universal healthcare for children and expand New York's Essential Plan so more families can afford the care they need. Proud sponsor of the NY Health Act.

As a member of the Bi-Partisan Choice Caucus, he voted for the New York State Equal Rights Amendment—guaranteeing a woman's right to choose in the State Constitution. He wrote and passed legislation to expand IVF coverage for women. He has been endorsed every year by Planned Parenthood Empire State Acts.

Built on a belief in the “Three P's”: Prevention, Policy, and Punishment. Authored the Homicide Witness Protection Act and the Car Theft Prevention Act. Earned the support of local law enforcement and has been designated a "Gun Sense Candidate" every year by Mom's Demand Action.
As Transportation Committee Chair, fighting for 125+ mph service connecting NYC to Toronto through Rochester. Secured $500K for a Thruway corridor feasibility study.
Led the Democratic Majority's first Regenerative Upstate Cities Initiative — driving workforce development, modern infrastructure, and downtown revitalization across all of Upstate New York.
Champion for public education and higher educational opportunities. A public school graduate who believes in guaranteeing a quality education regardless of the zip code you live in.

Authored the NY CHIPS Act bringing Micron and semiconductor jobs to Upstate. Introduced the Remote Worker Grant Program and fights for good-paying union jobs, workforce training, and fair wages across the district.

Committed to implementing the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act (CLCPA) — driving clean energy investment, reducing emissions, and ensuring environmental justice for frontline communities across New York.

Prioritizing the safety and modernization of existing energy infrastructure while holding utilities accountable. Focused on transitioning New York toward a clean energy future without sacrificing reliability or jobs.
